subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Paediatric solid tumours: neuroblastoma, Wilms, retinoblastoma and beyond

steps.tx: Sympathetic neuroendocrine neoplasms represent the most frequent solid neoplasms in infants. **Neuroblastoma** is the most common **extracranial solid tumour** of infancy, originating from neural crest sympathoadrenal progenitor cells in the adrenal medulla or sympathetic chain. Clinical presentation ranges from incidental asymptomatic masses to extensive retroperitoneal tumours causing vascular encasement, proptosis from orbital metastases, and subcutaneous blueberry muffin nodules.
steps.say: Sympathetic neuroendocrine neoplasms represent the most frequent solid neoplasms in infants. left.title: Neuroblastoma Origins
points: Originates from neural crest sympathoadrenal lineage
Adrenal medulla (primary site in ~50% of cases)
Paraspinal retroperitoneum, mediastinum, or neck
Secretes catecholamine metabolites: VMA and HVA

right.title: Clinical Manifestations
points: Abdominal mass crossing anatomical midline
Dumbbell extension into spinal canal causing cord compression
Periorbital ecchymosis and proptosis (raccoon eyes)
Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia paraneoplastic syndrome

steps.tx: Genomic copy number evaluation provides definitive risk categorization in neuroblastoma. **MYCN proto-oncogene** amplification greater than **4**-fold on chromosome 2p24 is the most powerful molecular marker of **high-risk neuroblastoma**, predicting rapid disease progression and chemotherapy resistance across all age groups. Additional adverse genomic features include 1p deletion, 11q deletion, and diploid karyotypes, which mandate intensified multimodal chemotherapy, tandem autologous transplantation, and radiation.

steps.tx: Monoclonal antibody targeting of surface gangliosides eliminates microscopic residual neuroblasts. **Dinutuximab** **anti-GD2** chimeric monoclonal antibody targeting disialoganglioside GD2 combined with GM-CSF, interleukin-**2**, and oral isotretinoin significantly improves event-free and overall survival in high-risk neuroblastoma in ANBL00**32**. Because GD2 is co-expressed on peripheral sensory nerve fibers, intravenous dinutuximab infusion triggers intense neuropathic pain requiring continuous intravenous opioid analgesia.
steps.say: Monoclonal antibody targeting of surface gangliosides eliminates microscopic residual neuroblasts. Dinutuximab anti-GD2 chimeric monoclonal antibody targeting disialoganglioside GD2 combined with GM-CSF, interleukin-2, and oral isotretinoin significantly improves survival in high-risk neuroblastoma in ANBL0032. Because GD2 is expressed on nerve fibers, it requires continuous opioid analgesia for pain.

steps.tx: Embryonal renal neoplasms arise through disruption of critical nephrogenic transcription factors. **Wilms tumour** nephroblastoma is the most common paediatric renal malignancy, strongly associated with **WT1 mutations** on chromosome **11**p**13** in WAGR and Denys-Drash syndromes. Characterized by triphasic histology comprising blastemal, epithelial, and stromal cells, the presence of diffuse anaplasia driven by somatic TP53 loss represents the single most adverse prognostic factor.

rows: Early diffuse mesangial sclerosis, male pseudohermaphroditism
~5-10% risk; screened with AFP & renal US

steps.tx: Neuroretinal malignancies illustrate the paradigm of biallelic tumour suppressor gene loss. **Retinoblastoma** arises from biallelic inactivation of the RB**1** tumour suppressor gene on chromosome **13**q**14**, presenting classically as **leukocoria** cat eye reflex and strabismus in early childhood. Modern eye-preserving therapy utilizes selective ophthalmic artery intra-arterial chemotherapy with melphalan, achieving globe salvage rates exceeding 80% while avoiding external beam radiation.

steps.tx: Embryonal liver neoplasms correlate with somatic and germline imprinting abnormalities. **Hepatoblastoma** is the most common liver malignancy in infants and young children, associated with **Beckwith-Wiedemann** syndrome and familial adenomatous polyposis, presenting with markedly elevated serum AFP. Cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy achieves high objective response rates, shrinking primary tumours to permit complete surgical resection or orthotopic liver transplantation.

left.title: Hepatoblastoma Features
points: Peak incidence in infants aged 6 months to 3 years
Associated with 11p15 imprinting & APC gene defects
Markedly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
Extreme chemosensitivity to cisplatin-based regimens

right.title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Children
points: Older children and adolescents (age > 10 years)
Associated with viral hepatitis B/C or metabolic cirrhosis
Lower sensitivity to systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy
Prognosis relies heavily on upfront R0 surgical resectability

steps.tx: Myogenic childhood soft tissue sarcomas segregate by characteristic histological and cytogenetic profiles. **Rhabdomyosarcoma** is the most common soft tissue sarcoma of childhood, divided histologically into favourable embryonal RMS with chromosome **11**p**15** loss of heterozygosity and high-risk **alveolar RMS** with FOXO**1** translocations. Fusion-positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma harbouring t(2;13) or t(1;13) translocations carries an aggressive natural history with early bone marrow and central nervous system metastases.
steps.say: Myogenic childhood soft tissue sarcomas segregate by characteristic histological and cytogenetic profiles. Rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common soft tissue sarcoma of childhood, divided histologically into favourable embryonal RMS with chromosome 11p15 loss of heterozygosity and high-risk alveolar RMS with FOXO1 translocations. left.title: Embryonal RMS (11p15 Loss)
points: Most common subtype (~70% of pediatric cases)
Favourable anatomical sites: orbit, head/neck, genitourinary
Triphasic spindled cells with rhabdomyoblasts
5-year overall survival exceeds 75% to 80%

right.title: Alveolar RMS (FOXO1 Fusion)
points: t(2;13) PAX3-FOXO1 or t(1;13) PAX7-FOXO1
Unfavourable extremity and trunk muscle predilection
Uniform small round cells forming pseudo-alveolar clefts
High risk of distant bone marrow dissemination

steps.tx: Primitive embryonal posterior fossa neoplasms require aggressive multimodal craniospinal treatment. **Medulloblastoma** standard management combines maximal safe surgical resection, **craniospinal irradiation**, and multi-agent platinum-alkylator chemotherapy, with cure rates exceeding **70%** in standard-risk disease. Craniospinal irradiation treats microscopic neuroaxial CSF seeding, while molecular subgrouping into WNT, SHH, Group 3, and Group 4 directs modern risk-adapted therapy de-escalation.
